notes: Each configuration keeps its checked-in machine types and timing.
Remote results measure host-wide counters and network wire bytes, including protocol overhead.
A single remote pass is a baseline observation, not a statistical performance ranking.
Standalone finite timings include process startup, gzip decoding, and input streaming.
Continuous file rates observe the configured generator load; they do not measure maximum throughput.
File-output comparisons include different wire formats and compression; outgoing network traffic cannot rank logical payload throughput.
Disk-buffer configurations use different synchronization policies, including per-event Logstash checkpoints and a 500ms Vector synchronization interval.
Disk/network average rates are means of already-normalized dstat rate samples; dividing their sum by the endpoint timestamp span would overstate rates.
Fluentd HTTP performance uses buffered bulk requests; its earlier per-event connection configuration exhausted local source ports under high concurrency and is excluded.
Splunk fixtures route background inputs to a disabled output group and fixture input to the active receiver.
The producer workload runs for 60 seconds; dstat capture also includes orchestration overhead. Actual sample counts and epoch spans are retained in provenance and comparison JSON.
